note.note:
Action Plan:
1) Arrange in-person clinic appointment (patient to book via app). Handover of today’s history to clinic team so the patient does not need to repeat details.
2) Perform focused physical examination at the visit: cardiovascular and respiratory assessment (heart and breathing) given palpitations and shortness of breath at rest.
3) Order thyroid blood tests at the visit to assess thyroxine control (thyroid function tests per doctor’s plan).
4) Defer starting any new medications until after in-person assessment and lab review.
5) Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Reason for visit/current issues:
  - Severe headaches affecting work; intermittent; occur mostly at work during meetings/laptop use; frontal; do not radiate; sometimes mild nausea.
  - Reduced appetite with unintentional ~5 lb weight loss (not intentional; no change in clothing fit; no external comments).
  - Tingling in both hands/arms described as quick “pricking”; no leg symptoms; new onset.
  - Palpitations (heart beating fast), about once daily or more; sometimes when entering the elevator in the morning.
  - Shortness of breath while sitting at desk; not with exercise.
  - Decreased libido, onset around same time as job change.
  - Symptoms began roughly when he changed jobs; occur at different times (not all together); usually at work.
  - Occupational stress rated 7–8/10; lawyer in London; work mix ~50% meetings and 50% computer/reading.
- Past medical history:
  - Patient reports “hyperthyroidism.”
- Medications:
  - Thyroxine (levothyroxine) — dose/route/frequency not documented; patient reports good adherence.
- Social history:
  - Alcohol: a couple of glasses of wine once weekly.
  - Non-smoker. No recreational drug use reported.
- Allergies:
  - Not documented.
- Other:
  - “Feeling hot” was listed in initial note; patient did not clearly endorse heat intolerance during the call and instead emphasized shortness of breath (see Quality checks).

Objective:
- Telemedicine encounter; no vitals or in-person examination performed today.
- No investigations completed yet.

Assessment & Plan:
1. Headaches:
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Tension-type headache.
   - Differential diagnosis:
     - Tension-type headache (DDx: Medium) — frontal, work/screen-associated, stress-related.
     - Work-related anxiety/panic with somatic symptoms (DDx: High) — stress temporal pattern; may exacerbate headaches.
     - Migraine without aura (DDx: in VINDICATE) — episodic with mild nausea; fewer migrainous features documented.
     - Cervicogenic/postural strain (DDx: in T) — prolonged reading/computer work.
     - Carbon monoxide or building-related exposure (DDx: Low–Medium) — headaches largely at work; no coworker cluster reported.
   - Investigations planned: None prior to in-person; assessment to occur at clinic visit.
   - Treatment planned: Defer until post-exam and labs.

2. Reduced appetite and unintentional weight loss (~5 lb):
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Work-related stress effect.
   - Differential diagnosis:
     - Thyroid dysfunction/over-replacement (DDx: Medium).
     - Nutritional deficiency or anemia (B12 or iron deficiency) (DDx: Low).
     - Building-related exposure (DDx: Low–Medium) — less typical for isolated weight change.
   - Investigations planned: Thyroid blood tests at clinic visit.
   - Treatment planned: To be determined post-evaluation.

3. Tingling in both hands/arms:
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Hyperventilation/anxiety-related paresthesias.
   - Differential diagnosis:
     - Hyperventilation-induced paresthesias (DDx: in T).
     - Vitamin B12 deficiency (DDx: in D) — bilateral paresthesias possible.
   - Investigations planned: To be considered after initial clinic assessment; no tests ordered today per transcript.
   - Treatment planned: To be determined post-evaluation.

4. Palpitations:
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Work-related anxiety/panic episodes.
   - Differential diagnosis:
     - Work-related anxiety/panic (DDx: High).
     - Thyroid dysfunction/over-replacement (DDx: Medium).
     - Iron-deficiency anemia (DDx: in D) — less supported without exertional symptoms.
   - Investigations planned: In-person cardiovascular exam at clinic visit; thyroid blood tests.
   - Treatment planned: Defer pending exam and labs.

5. Shortness of breath at rest (desk), not with exercise:
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Anxiety/hyperventilation related to work setting.
   - Differential diagnosis:
     - Work-related anxiety/panic (DDx: High).
     - Thyroid dysfunction/over-replacement (DDx: Medium).
     - Carbon monoxide/indoor air quality exposure (DDx: Low–Medium).
   - Investigations planned: In-person respiratory and cardiovascular examination at clinic visit; thyroid blood tests.
   - Treatment planned: Defer pending exam and labs.

6. Decreased libido:
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Stress-related change.
   - Differential diagnosis:
     - Thyroid dysfunction (DDx: Medium).
     - Pituitary adenoma/prolactinoma (DDx: Low) — no visual changes/galactorrhea documented.
   - Investigations planned: Thyroid blood tests (as above).
   - Treatment planned: To be determined post-evaluation.

7. Thyroid disease on thyroxine:
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Thyroid status unclear; patient reports “hyperthyroidism” but is on levothyroxine.
   - Differential diagnosis:
     - Iatrogenic hyperthyroidism from over-replacement (DDx: Medium).
     - Underlying hypothyroidism on replacement (history wording unclear) — conflict noted with patient-stated history.
   - Investigations planned: Thyroid blood tests at clinic visit.
   - Treatment planned: Adjust management after lab results and clinical review.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements:
  - Allergy status not documented.
  - Medication dose/route/frequency not documented for thyroxine.
  - No vitals or physical examination today (tele-visit).
  - No standardized anxiety screening documented (e.g., GAD-7) — not performed in transcript.
- Internal conflicts (conflict noted):
  - Patient reports “hyperthyroidism” but is taking thyroxine (levothyroxine), typically used for hypothyroidism.
  - Initial note referenced “feeling hot,” but patient did not clearly endorse heat intolerance during the call and emphasized shortness of breath instead.
- Transcript quality:
  - Occasional pauses/inaudible segments; overall history understandable and coherent.
